topic: Static source, goal and path called adjuncts
claim: Of [35] (The house faces towards the forest; The road runs from the village to the castle; The track winds its way along the banks of the river): “These do not involve any change of location, but express static situations. The adjuncts are therefore not bounding.”
evidence_summary: Page 692 (§5.3) says spatial extent elements “have the properties of complements”, and that “Extent complements do not have this effect with stative clauses: examples like [4] are unbounded”. [4ii] (p. 691) is The road runs along the river for 20 miles, with the same static run as [35iii], and p. 690 says the endpoints in [35iii] “define an extent of space”. Page 684 says change-of-location dependents “are normally complements”, and p. 685 says the x’s way idiom licenses them, which covers [35v].
finding: Medium-high confidence. The same kind of element is an adjunct on p. 689 and a complement on p. 692, and p. 665 defines “adjunct” so as to exclude complements. A defence that static face or broaden out doesn’t license its PP fails for [35iii], with the run of [4ii], and for [35v]. Compare CG-0113 and CG-0134.
proposed_wording: These elements are therefore not bounding.
inference: Are the static source, goal and path elements in [35] adjuncts?

evidence.passage: §4.4, p. 689. “The adjuncts are therefore not bounding.”
evidence.example: Page 691 [4ii] The road runs along the river for 20 miles; p. 692, “Extent complements”.
evidence.establishes: The chapter calls the same kind of static element an adjunct and a complement.
